The PR touches only username/locale; OpenmrsFilter.java:64 still does httpRequest.setAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID, String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis())). `git grep -n INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID` in the worktree at d381957e returns exactly two hits (WebConstants.java:20 definition, OpenmrsFilter.java:64 write) and no reader, with a positive control proving the pipeline works (`git grep -c WebConstants -- web/src/main` returns hits) -- so the ticket is right that core reads it nowhere. But it is a published contract: `gh api search/code -f q='INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID org:openmrs'` returns total_count=10, including openmrs-module-legacyui omod/.../taglib/HtmlIncludeTag.java and omod/.../controller/PortletController.java, openmrs-module-reporting ReportingPortletController.java, openmrs-module-htmlformflowsheet HtmlIncludeTag.java, openmrs-module-htmlwidgets HtmlUtil.java, openmrs-module-personalhr PortletController.java. claim: doFilterInternal_shouldUpdateChangedSessionAttributes seeds the stale locale as Locale.ENGLISH, which counts as 'changed' only because the ambient default locale happens to be en_GB; the test is silently coupled to the default_locale global property.

claim: Removing the unconditional per-request setAttribute calls also removes the incidental per-request dirty-marking of the HttpSession, so authorization-relevant state that is mutated in place on the session-stored UserContext (refreshAuthenticatedUser reloading roles/privileges, removeProxyPrivilege, setLocationId) may no longer be persisted or replicated by session stores that only save on attribute change; was a clustered / externally-stored-session deployment considered?
evidence: The UserContext is written to the session only on creation (OpenmrsFilter.java:76-81, unchanged); every later change is an in-place mutation of that same object. api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/UserContext.java:50 declares `public class UserContext implements Serializable`, so it is intended to survive a replicating/persisting session store, and lines 152 (refreshAuthenticatedUser -> reloads the User, i.e. roles and privileges, without changing getUsername()), 264/319 (removeProxyPrivilege) and 578 (setLocationId) all mutate authorization-relevant state without changing the `username` or `locale` values this PR now compares against. Before this change every request executed `setAttribute("username", ...)` and `setAttribute("locale", ...)` (base version, git show eda229b1:.../OpenmrsFilter.java lines 75 and 94), which marked the session dirty every request; at d381957e a steady-state request performs zero writes -- I confirmed this empirically with a probe extending BaseWebContextSensitiveTest that recorded setAttribute calls (second request on an unchanged authenticated session: writes=[]; the PR's own OpenmrsFilterTest#doFilterInternal_shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes asserts the same, 5/5 green via `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest`). Counter-evidence I found and am reporting honestly: `git grep -n distributable` over the tree returns nothing (positive control: the same `git grep` pipeline finds 'anonymous user' in 4 files), webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:375-379 has a session-config with only a cookie-config, `git grep -in 'session replicat|PersistentManager|DeltaManager|BackupManager|spring-session|SessionRepository'` returns nothing, and the TRUNK-6701 description itself frames the redundant locale write as a *problem* ('marking the session dirty for replicating session managers'). Also, per-attribute delta managers (Tomcat DeltaManager, Spring Session's delta map) only ever replicated the `username`/`locale` keys, never the userContext key, so for those the gap pre-dates this PR; it is only full-session-on-dirty managers (e.g. Tomcat BackupManager) where this is a change.
